implementation_notes: JavaScript has no interface construct, so the contract is the set of messages a collaborator must answer and injection through a constructor or a module parameter replaces the classic structure entirely. JSDoc's @interface/@implements tags (or a TypeScript checker over JSDoc, tsc --checkJs) document and partially check that contract without creating any runtime object. Keep a hand-written abstract base class only when a runtime marker (instanceof) or shared default behaviour is genuinely needed.
pitfalls: Nothing enforces the contract at runtime: a collaborator missing a method fails only when the call happens.
JSDoc @interface is inert unless a checker (tsc --checkJs or an IDE) runs in CI.
Passing a class instead of an instance, or losing this by extracting a method, satisfies the shape while failing at call time.
